label: Process
description: An instance of a running program with its own memory space and resources.

label: Thread
description: A lightweight unit of execution within a process, sharing its memory and resources.

label: Context Switch
description: The act of saving and restoring CPU state when switching between processes or threads.

label: Scheduler
description: The operating system component that decides which process or thread runs next.

label: Interrupt
description: A signal to the CPU that temporarily halts execution to handle an event.

label: System Call
description: A controlled entry point for user programs to request services from the operating system.

label: File Descriptor
description: An integer handle used by the OS to reference open files, sockets, or devices.

label: Virtual Memory
description: An abstraction that provides processes with the illusion of a large, contiguous memory space.

label: Page
description: A fixed-size block of memory used in virtual memory systems.

label: Page Fault
description: An event triggered when a process accesses a page not currently in physical memory.

label: Semaphore
description: A synchronization primitive used to control access to shared resources.

label: Mutex
description: A lock mechanism ensuring only one thread accesses a resource at a time.

label: Deadlock
description: A situation where processes or threads wait indefinitely for resources held by each other.

label: Race Condition
description: An error that occurs when the outcome depends on the timing of concurrent operations.

label: Kernel
description: The core part of the operating system that manages hardware and system resources.

label: Device Driver
description: Software that allows the operating system to communicate with hardware devices.

label: Signal
description: An asynchronous notification sent to a process to trigger predefined handling.

label: IPC
description: Inter-Process Communication mechanisms like pipes, sockets, and shared memory.

label: Bootloader
description: A small program that loads the operating system kernel into memory at startup.

label: Privilege Level
description: Defines the access rights of code running on the CPU, such as user mode or kernel mode.
